items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: "Just because I gave you free lessons doesn't mean you're obliged to do it." I said, "Okay, Mr. Gallagher, okay."

ctx.x: Scotch or Irish by any means but I've always loved the bagpipes. When I first came to New York, people asked me what I was, I'd say American. And that's not a good answer in New York, you know. In New York you've got to be an ethnic. So they'd say, "You've got a Scottish name, you must be Scottish. So I decided I'd be Scottish. Some of my ancestors did come from Scotland and I did hear a lot about it around the house, I heard some Scottish words, you know. I guess if there were any two outstanding cultures it…

But I would go to hear these pipe bands when they'd come to the Garden and tears would pour out of my eyes. So my wife bought me some pipes about 30 years ago and I went to a teacher and learned to play them. And it was kind of funny, in the beginning he gave me free lessons, he wouldn't take any money. And it came around January and he said, well, it's time to be measured up for the kilt. I said, I don't want a kilt, I just want to play the bagpipes. He said, well, you don't have to march in the parade but you…
